title: resolve_lora_path() receives args.lora_path as a LIST (action="append") but expects a string — crashes with TypeError whenever --lora-path is set
detail: args.lora_path is registered with action="append" (multi-LoRA support), so it is always a list. Several command call sites pass args.lora_path straight into resolve_lora_path(), which expects a scalar string path. Result: TypeError / crash the moment a user sets --lora-path. Confirmed across FIVE files in one scan: image-controlnet.py:437 and :190 (run_controlnet fingerprint path), image-expansion.py:323, image-profile.py:777, image-workflow.py:876. This is the single largest hotspot family in the codebase (5 of 10 findings, 5 of 5 critical). Fix shape: index the list (args.lora_path[0] or iterate) or make resolve_lora_path accept a list.

title: Unguarded default=None on a flag silently wins over _shared's intended concrete default (e.g. default=777) on the unified image parser
detail: image-profile.py:149 registers --seed with default=None but does NOT guard it, so the None silently overrides the _shared default=777 on the unified image parser. This is the same sentinel-pattern bug family already documented in MEMORY (argparse-sentinel-for-user-override): a per-command flag without a guard (default=None treated as 'unset') collides with the shared parser's concrete default. Here it manifests as the shared default being shadowed rather than as a magic-number override, but the root cause — missing guard so the per-command registration participates in arg resolution — is identical. One finding (medium) but expected to recur wherever a subcommand re-declares a shared flag.

title: Subcommand registers shared flags (--lora-path/--lora-scale/--prompt/--seed) WITHOUT guards, relying on _shared's LATER skip to dedupe — order-coupled and fragile
detail: video-generate.py:192 declares --lora-path/--lora-scale/--prompt/--seed unguarded and depends on _shared.add_common_generation_args() skipping already-registered flags when it runs afterward. Correctness hinges entirely on registration ORDER (subcommand before _shared) and on _shared's skip logic being present. If _shared ever runs first, or its skip is removed/changed, these become argparse 'conflicting option' errors or silent double-registration. This is an architectural smell, not a live crash today. Related: video.py:113 has a comment claiming --self-test is registered by add_common_generation_args() but video.py never calls that function — a stale/misleading comment in the same family.

title: Help text advertises a default that differs from the actual argparse default — misleading --help, no runtime bug
detail: image-anime2real.py:156: --realism-style help string claims '3d-game (default)' but the actual argparse default is civitai-chinese. Pure documentation drift — help text was not updated when the default changed. No runtime impact, but erodes trust in --help and the schema-defaults reflection. Low severity; grep for '(default)' in help strings when a default is intentionally changed.

title: Reshape/downsample expressions that assume dims are exact multiples of the latent grid, hidden behind an obfuscated one-liner
detail: flux2_outpaint_pipeline.py:330: mask downsample reshape assumes spatial dims are exact multiples of the latent grid, but the expression is written as an obfuscated one-liner that hides the divisibility assumption. If a caller passes dims that are NOT clean multiples (e.g. odd outpaint targets), the reshape silently produces wrong-shaped tensors or crashes with a cryptic error. Refactor to an explicit assert or floor-div with a comment stating the invariant. Low severity because current call paths happen to satisfy it; latent trap for future callers.

title: review-optimize scan coverage: full-scope scan reaches 26 files / 22165 lines; correctness + argparse-integrity are the live dimensions, lora-path is the dominant hotspot
detail: Run 2026-06-18T14-11-24 (review-only, full scope) scanned 26 files / 22165 lines across layers entry(1)+commands(18)+core(8). Produced 10 findings, all 10 verified and new (0 suppressed from prior — first run on this knowledge file). Dimension split: correctness=7, argparse-integrity=3.
